question: On real Arabic web text, does one-pass (offline) gradient-alignment filtering toward a downstream Arabic task beat random sampling for LoRA adaptation of Qwen2.5-1.5B when the full cost of scoring the pool is charged to the filter?
motivation: Stages 68-72 selected online among four synthetic-mixture candidates per step, with a Wikipedia language-modelling target. Practical data selection (e.g. LESS, CoLoR-Filter) is usually offline: score a real pool once toward a downstream task, keep the top fraction, then train. The scoring cost is then a fixed charge rather than a per-step ratio.
hardware: The Colab GPU of this session, NVIDIA L4 (no A100 available on 24 November 2026). Device journaled with the calibration; resuming on a different device type aborts.
model: Qwen2.5-1.5B (revision and weight SHA-256 as in research/llm-gpu-scale-protocol.json). Numerics, LoRA (rank 8, alpha 16, q_proj and v_proj) and AdamW (lr 5e-4, weight decay 0) as stages 69-72; one 65-token chunk per update.
software: transformers 4.46.3, tokenizers 0.20.3, huggingface_hub 0.26.2 (as the stage 69-72 notebooks); torch and CUDA as preinstalled, journaled.

web_data.source: HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-2, dataset revision af9c13333eb981300149d5ca60a8e9d659b276b9, license ODC-By.
web_data.kept_file: data/arb_Arab/test/000_00000.parquet, SHA-256 a84851f790551b08c141eab938448961812582629dbbabc737d997d519b3ed39 (42,080 documents that passed the FineWeb-2 filters).
web_data.removed_file: data/arb_Arab_removed/train/000_00000.parquet, SHA-256 2c3b8cf5ad625369fffbab09ba7b6dc81578c436216fd5a29ce547f8eeb29295; only the first 20 row groups (20,000 documents removed by the FineWeb-2 filters) are read.
web_data.chunk: First 65 Qwen tokens (no special tokens) of each document with at least 65 tokens, in file order.
web_data.decontamination: Before sampling, drop every chunk that shares any token 8-gram with the tokenized text (prompt plus correct continuation) of any probe or target item. Counts journaled.
web_data.pools: kept sample = 2048 eligible kept chunks drawn without replacement (default_rng(7311)); removed sample = 1024 eligible removed chunks (default_rng(7312)). Pool 'kept' = the 2048 kept chunks. Pool 'raw' = the first 1024 kept chunks in draw order plus the 1024 removed chunks (M = 2048, removed share 0.5). The 0.5 share approximates the natural proportion: FineWeb-2 arb_Arab has 28 removed and 25 kept training files of about 4.8 GB each (removed byte share 0.53).

task.source: MBZUAI/ArabicMMLU, revision 7aa530e2893ac420352b3f5c1a1310c010e9758b, license CC BY-NC 4.0; files All/dev.csv (SHA-256 3c72bd01f3acf6c1ed8acf28ba344ea739fcf9ee7f999802ced958e3b4d8b5dc, 120 items) and All/test.csv (SHA-256 c4ba4d6c6903d2b7b4415f18c9bb3173ba55c1344a91339769deba931d0c2782, 14,455 items). Not used in any earlier stage.
task.format: Cloze. Prompt = (Context + newline, if present) + 'سؤال: ' + Question + newline + 'الجواب:'; continuation = ' ' + option text. Prompt and continuation are tokenized separately and concatenated; prompt truncated from the left to 192 tokens, continuation to its first 64 tokens. Options are the non-empty Option 1-5 fields; Answer Key A-E gives the correct one.
task.item_loss: Mean token cross-entropy of the correct continuation given the prompt.

policies.random: Each step trains on a pool chunk drawn uniformly with replacement.
policies.align_grad: Once, at the seed's initial adapter: probe gradient g_p of the mean probe item loss; per-example LoRA gradients of all 2048 pool chunks from batched backward passes (batch 16, experiments.llm_budget.PerExampleCapture); score_i = <g_i, g_p>. Keep the 512 highest scores (ties by lower index). Each step then trains on a kept chunk drawn uniformly with replacement.
policies.align_fd: Not a training arm (see amendment). Forward-only approximation of the same score: u = g_p / ||g_p||; score_i = [L_i(theta + eps u) - L_i(theta - eps u)] / (2 eps), eps = 0.01, from no-grad batched forwards (batch 16). Computed once in the calibration on the raw pool for its cost and its agreement with align_grad.

sign_convention: A descent step on chunk i changes the probe loss by about -lr <g_i, g_p>, so the largest scores are kept.
schedule: Per pool index k (kept 0, raw 1) and seed: rng = default_rng(seed + 1000 k); random indices = rng.integers(2048, size=B); filter indices = rng.integers(512, size=B), mapped into the align_grad kept set.
budget: Before any target evaluation: calibration with seed 73999 on the raw pool. c_r = median of steps 5-24 of 24 random steps with CUDA synchronisation; S_grad and S_fd = wall-clock of the complete scoring of the 2048 raw-pool chunks (probe gradient included). Budget B = 2400 random-step costs; N_grad = floor(B - S_grad / c_r + 1e-9). If N_grad < 1 the arm is reported as infeasible. Costs and N_grad are journaled before the main runs.
measurement: Every run trains B updates. Target loss and accuracy at step 0 and B for both arms, and at N_grad for both. Journaled per filter run: all 2048 scores, the kept indices and the share of removed chunks among them; scoring wall-clock per run. Journaled in the calibration: both score vectors of seed 73999 on the raw pool, their Spearman correlation and kept-set overlap.
primary: Raw pool: align_grad target loss at N_grad minus random at B (cost charged), mean over six seeds, paired seed-bootstrap 95% interval (seed 7303, 10000 resamples). Negative favours the filter.
prediction: Written before running. Raw pool: align_grad minus random negative (removed share 0.5 exceeds the stage-71 crossover 0.34), with low confidence because the scoring charge here is a fixed fraction of the budget rather than the stage-71 ratio. Kept pool: positive (random better), as for curated in-domain pools in stage 70.
secondary: Both pools, charged (align_grad at N_grad minus random at B) and amortized (align_grad at B minus random at B); selection term (align_grad at N_grad minus random at N_grad) and throughput term; random minus no update; accuracy contrasts (argmax over options of mean continuation log-probability); removed share among kept chunks (raw pool); measured S_grad / c_r and S_fd / c_r; fd-versus-grad agreement in the calibration. Paired seed-bootstrap intervals; no multiplicity adjustment; no pooling across pools.
resumption: Journal (JSON lines) outside the repository during the run; completed (pool, seed, arm) entries are skipped; pools, target sample and schedule digests re-verified against the calibration entry.
coverage: 2 pools x 6 seeds x 2 arms = 24 runs plus one calibration.
audit: tools/audit_llm_web_filter.py: journal digest, summary recomputation, file hashes, decontamination, samples and pools, schedules, kept sets recomputed from journaled scores, removed shares, budget from journaled costs. On the same GPU: recompute align_grad scores for 256 pool chunks of seed 37300 on both pools and compare to the journal (relative tolerance 1e-4), and replay the first 50 random-arm steps of seed 37300 on the raw pool to its step-50 adapter digest.
scope: One model, LoRA, one budget, one kept fraction (0.25), one web shard per filter class, a pool of 2048 chunks, one downstream task scored as loss (not generation). FineWeb-2's own filter labels are used only to build the raw pool and to measure what the alignment filter keeps, not as a competing arm.
amendment_before_outcomes: Amended on 24 November 2026 before any target evaluation; see research/llm-web-filter-deviations.md. A smoke test on train candidates and dev items (no test items) measured: random step 0.110 s; scoring 512 raw-pool chunks 34.5 s (align_grad) and 33.4 s (align_fd); probe gradient about 7 s; evaluation 0.086 s per item. The original design (M 4096, B 1600, target 1024, three arms) would have made both filters infeasible (scoring 4096 chunks about 1,900 random steps) and taken about 10 hours. Changes: M 4096 -> 2048, kept 1024 -> 512, B 1600 -> 2400, target 1024 -> 512 items, align_fd dropped as a training arm (it costs the same as align_grad) and kept as a calibration-only measurement, fd batch 64 -> 16 (out-of-memory retries at 64). Seeds, pools' construction, task, model and primary contrast are unchanged.
